description: Studied the agentic coding workflows of experienced developers in the Foundation Interface Lab under Haijun Xia.

Started my research career in the applied sociology field with Amy Donley, eventually leading the UMOR project after a year of collaboration. Joined the Socio-Technical Interaction Research Lab under Pamela Wisniewski shortly after to help with the IGDD project, which then turned into MOSafely. Later worked with Jonathan Powell to maintain CoupCast and wrote some articles with Salah Ben Hammou, his PhD student at the time.

Placed in the Computer-Enabled Abilities Laboratory under Brian Smith to build prototypes that integrate spatial interactions into desktop screen readers and support face-to-face help between sighted and blind strangers exploring physical spaces.
Applied TDA algorithms on ACS datasets from Mecklenburg County to identify communities of interest. Collaborated with Jim Thatcher and Courtney Thatcher from the University of Puget Sound.
